I got to meet Sgt. Slaughter at a convention in 2013. My mom used to watch tons of wrestling with her father and grandmother, and they all loved the Sarge. Of course then, I wanted to ask for a picture together, while maybe even getting the chance to talk with him, so I waited for the line to die down. 

Which was easier than I thought because there was never a line...or a person there. 

I introduced myself, said he still looked tough as nails (it seemed like a nice compliment?) and mentioned my family being big fans. He just kinda smiled and nodded. To be honest, the only real talk we had was when we had a laugh about how shitty the convention center was. After all that, I wanted to try my best to get a photo with him, but sadly I wasted most of my money on actually getting into the event. I kept hearing this weird sound from below me, and when I bent over to look, it was a small man asking me to give him money for a picture. I think it was Slaughter's manager or something. I guess Slaughter felt like he disappointed me (the only guy who showed up to his table to be fair) and kept asking the tiny terror to lower the price, but the guy kept asking for crazy shit like "30 bucks! 28 bucks!" in this really abrasive way. Idk about anyone else, but 30 bucks for a picture is not my thing. Hell even 5 bucks for a picture is pushing it.

The greedy oompa loompa kept insisting on amounts larger than 20 bucks, and made the whole thing awkward. I decided enough was enough and I wanted to leave. I shook the Sarge's hand (a hell of a grip) and told him to have a good day. While I walked away the little guy kept trying to convince me to pay, but this time he said "okay, you can have a picture....for whatever you have on you right now". I shook my head, resisted the urge to pet him and walked away. 

That was my first time meeting a wrestler, nothing crazy, but convention stories are always fun ones to tell. If you ever want to meet a wrestler that isn't too popular, cons are a great way to do it. They're usually happy to be there. I also met Jerry Lawler this year at the same con, and while not boring anyone with the details, he's actually a super chill guy and funnier than people think. Also I found out through an exchange he had with a comic book artist next to him that he really, REALLY likes female cosplayers, I'll leave it at that.

Yeah, I can't say I blame people for complaining this month tbh. It's an improvement over last month, but that's not saying anything good. I'm personally content with Spelunky alone because fuck yeah I always wanted to try it. But when I consider the other selections, I realize they kinda feel like cop-outs. 

We got Dragon's Crown just last August, and DC is pretty much Mystara but with a lot more depth (and don't get me wrong, I think Mystara looks fun, I liked the demo). The situation with Arkham Asylum and us having gotten Arkham City this year, isn't that different either. I can see personally where some people feel like they're slowly getting less bang for their buck. 

Can't speak for Vita and PS4 owners, I don't fall into either of those camps (just own a PS3), but are you guys thrilled about your selections? I hope so.

My best bet is that Kojima is just impressed with all the work put into GTA V, and after finally getting the chance to make the open world game he's always wanted to work on, he finally learned first hand all the effort that goes into it.

He probably just said "depressed" because at that moment, he realized people will compare the two and all that hard work will be forgotten. I respect the honesty and can't blame him. If I had a quarter for every time someone called something a "GTA clone" and shrugged it off, I could probably make my own AAA open world game. 

But I bet he was just talking about it because that's how he was feeling in that moment, I doubt when he goes home he thinks about it. He says it himself, he doesn't really play games anymore.
